metadata.title: Baghelkhand ka World Famous CHICKEN BAGHELI & DEHATI CHICKEN I RECIPE I Aalu Vanda + BEST Khurchan
metadata.description:

https://www.youtube.com/c/anubhavsapra

0:00 Introduction
0.31 Stepwise Preparation of Chicken Bagheli 
9:41 Tasting
12.36 Pandit Ji Mangodi Wale 
15:56 Rajput Dhaba & Sweets
18:06 The Street Kitchen

In today's episode we have come to Indian Curry Family Restaurant at Bypass Raipur Karchuliyan in Rewa to discover the story and taste of a famous meat dish from this region named Bagheli chicken whose origin was from the royal kitchen of Baghelkhand. This exploration also includes a short street food tour in the adjoining neighborhood along with our host gracious Shashak and Pramod Ji. 

Indian Curry Family Restaurant is a quaint eatery surrounded by pretty garden space that liven up the whole ambience. On reaching there we joined owner Pramod Ji for the making of this traditional dish. A quick overview from him made us realize that this dish is a rich and robust, red chilli, onion, garlic and spices based slow cooked meat curry which has a few quintessential characteristics. First it is cooked with lots of whole Indian spices that are toasted and powdered to form a spice mix. Secondly the chicken is marinated with red chilli garlic paste, curd, the spice mix and ginger garlic paste prior to cooking and third point is it is cooked slowly over wood or dung fire. All these make its taste stand out. 

Pramod Ji is a seasoned chef specializing in Bagheli cuisine and his knowledge about the history, traditions and the practices pertaining to different dishes is highly inspirational. First he patiently marinated the chicken with curd and spices and kept it aside. While doing so he enlightened us about the nuances of the process in a lucid manner. Next he prepared a paste with coriander, chilli, hand powdered garam masala and some store bought chicken masala and kept that side as well. Then he heated a cauldron over a stove and threw some whole garam masala into the ghee in it. This was followed by onions, ginger-garlic paste, marinated chicken and the masala paste. Then the whole thing was slowly and patiently cooked for a long time until the dish attained a reddish orange hue and the fat separated and settled on the surface giving a sheen to this semi dry dish. Throughout the process we picked up so many nitty gritties about the dish. 

Finally we joined a few other friends for tasting and were completely floored by the taste from the first morsel itself. The meat was well cooked and had soaked all the aroma of the garam masala and other ingredients. This dish tastes best with native chicken. After that we embarked on a quick street food tour in the adjoining locality. The first stop was Pandit Ji Mangodiwale whose fried snacks and chai is a hit with the locals. The non stop action of fritters being fried and chai being prepared in huge vessels seemed overwhelming. We tried some aalu bonda with chai and quite liked it. 

The second stop was Rajput Dhaba & Sweets where we tried their best selling khurchan. It was a luscious and creamy dessert consisting of a stack of thick malai sheets and these guys have clearly mastered the craft. The last stop of this food walk was The Street Kitchen run by a young fellow passionate to serve toothsome traditional dishes to the masses. Here we tried the dehati chicken, a rich curry that is prepared with mustard oil and whole spices. The flavours were amazing and so was the texture of the meat. 

We had a great time relishing these brilliant dishes from this place. Heartfelt thanks to all our hosts for their warm hospitality and insights.
